concepts.def: The plot of a text or film: what happens and in what order, including el desenlace, the ending or resolution.
Character study: el protagonista, el antagonista, and la caracterización - how the author or director builds and develops each figure.
The central ideas a work explores, such as la memoria histórica, la injusticia social, la libertad or las relaciones familiares.
Devices that create meaning: el narrador (narrator), el flashback, el simbolismo, and in film la banda sonora and el plano (shot).
The historical and social setting of the work, which illuminates why characters act as they do and what the author criticises.
Plan an introduction, develop arguments supported by specific scenes or quotations, and finish with a justified conclusion - analyse, do not retell.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Literary Texts and Films — a core area of A-Level Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Literary Texts and Films brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Literary Texts and Films.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In literary study, 'el argumento' means what?
options: The plot
An argument between characters
The book's price
The author's biography

mcqs.q: A strong essay paragraph about a text or film should do what?
options: Make a point and support it with a specific scene or quotation
Retell the whole story in order
List every character's name
Give only your personal feelings

mcqs.q: What is 'la banda sonora' of a film?
options: The soundtrack
The opening credits
The film poster
The subtitles

mcqs.q: 'El desenlace' of a story refers to what?
options: The ending or resolution
The list of chapters
The main setting
The publisher

mcqs.q: What does 'el argumento' mean when discussing a novel or film?
options: It means the cover design of the book.
The plot - the sequence of events in the work.
It means an argument or quarrel between the characters.
Symbolism only exists in silent films.

mcqs.q: Will retelling the story earn high marks in the essay?
options: No - marks come from analysing how themes, characters and techniques create meaning, supported by selected evidence.
It means the cover design of the book.
A detailed summary of the plot shows the examiner you know the work.
Essays are marked only on their length.

mcqs.q: Is symbolism only relevant when studying poetry?
options: Essays are marked only on their length.
No - films and novels use symbols and recurring motifs too, and directors add visual symbolism through images, colour and music.
Symbolism only exists in silent films.
Simbolismo belongs to poetry, so it is irrelevant to films.
